'''''Valeriana dioica''''', the '''marsh valerian''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Caprifoliaceae]], native to North America, Europe and Anatolia.<ref name="30028947-2" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:30028947-2 |title=''Valeriana dioica'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=28 December 2020}}</ref> It is typically found in calcareous fens.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Germination requirements of the subordinate fen meadow species ''Valeriana dioica'' L. |year=2019 |last1=Rasran |first1=Leonid |last2=Eisenmann |first2=Cornelia |last3=Wagentristl |first3=Regina |last4=Bernhardt |first4=Karl-Georg |journal=Folia Geobotanica |volume=54 |issue=1–2 |pages=125–138 |doi=10.1007/s12224-019-09354-3 |s2cid=208044334 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2019FolGe..54..125R }}</ref> It is a [[dioecious]] species, with male and female flowers on separate individuals, and it is pollinated by small flies.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.actao.2005.07.001 |title=Distance-dependent pollen limitation of seed set in some insect-pollinated dioecious plants |year=2005 |last1=De Jong |first1=Tom J. |last2=Batenburg |first2=Judith C. |last3=Klinkhamer |first3=Peter G.L. |journal=Acta Oecologica |volume=28 |issue=3 |pages=331–335 |bibcode=2005AcO....28..331D}}</ref>
